caption: A light switch is flicked up and down several times in quick succession, and the ceiling light goes on and off in step with each flick.

sa.check: A light switch and a ceiling light in the same room.
The switch is flicked up and down several times in quick succession.
The ceiling light goes on and off with the flicks.
There are several flicks, not one.
Each change of the light follows a flick.

pc.expect: Every flick changes the light's state at once: each time the switch moves the light goes from off to on or on to off.
pc.fail: The switch moves and the light stays as it was; or the light changes while the switch is still; or the light changes only after a delay while the switch has already moved again; or the light changes twice for one flick.

pc.expect: Between flicks the light holds its state; after the last flick it stays in that state for the rest of the clip.
pc.fail: The light flickers between flicks with the switch still; or changes state after the flicking has stopped; or dims gradually rather than switching; or the switch moves by itself.

pc.expect: The room brightens and darkens with the light: the walls and floor under the fixture follow each change.
pc.fail: The fixture goes dark while the room stays as bright; or the room changes brightness while the fixture stays as it was; or light stays pooled under the dark fixture.

pc.expect: Nothing else in the room moves as the switch is flicked; the fixture hangs still.
pc.fail: Doors or objects move at the flicks; or the fixture swings; or the switch plate slides on the wall.

pc.expect: One switch and one ceiling light; both stay in place; the hand passes through nothing.
pc.fail: A second switch or light appears; or the fixture vanishes or moves across the ceiling; or the hand passes into the wall; or the room's contents appear or vanish between lit and dark frames.

pc.expect: Everything in view, named in the caption or not, keeps its number, identity and shape unless something visible acts on it, and nothing passes through anything else.
pc.fail: An object that nothing visible acts on appears from nothing; or vanishes while still in frame and not occluded; or duplicates or merges with another; or turns into a different object or a different shape between frames; or any object passes through another. Changes brought about by the caption's event or by a visible interaction, objects leaving the frame, and occlusion are not failures.

pc.expect: The wall colour, the fixture and the room's contents stay the same apart from brightness.
pc.fail: The wall changes colour rather than brightness; or the fixture changes shape; or pictures or furniture change.
